title: mixed-slo-onboarding-playbook-for-quant-and-cache-sensitive-models
author: Marissa Chen
content:
## Summary

This playbook documents the onboarding, evaluation, and rollout process for models that must satisfy mixed SLOs across latency, token-cost, and semantic fidelity when deployed with quantized kernels and KV cache optimizations. It targets models that will run on Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private runtimes where quantization and cache behavior materially affect output quality or latency.

Audience: Model owners, inference engineers, SREs, and applied ML evaluators.

Goals:
- Define an acceptance matrix that balances latency SLO, per-token cost targets, and fidelity thresholds for prompt families.
- Provide reproducible eval harness recipes for quant-aware and cache-aware tests.
- Prescribe rollout and rollback steps (shadow -> canary -> prod) with telemetry gates and regression triage hooks.
- Document operational runbook for common cache/quant failure modes and mitigation.

---

## 1) Pre-onboarding checklist (owner: model-owner)

Ensure the following before any eval runs: 

- Model artifact is stored in Redwood artifact registry with semantic version and provenance metadata (model_name, commit_sha, training_checkpoint_id).
- Quantization metadata completed: algorithm (PTQ/QLoRA/HALF), bitwidth targets, per-layer calibration artifacts, and expected memory profile.
- KV cache semantics documented: indexing format (byte-level vs token-level), warmup strategy, and expected cache hit distributions for representative workloads.
- Representative prompt families selected (see Section 3) and a labeled probe seed of 2k–10k examples covering latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, and fidelity-sensitive slices.
- Ownership & oncall: two engineers assigned (primary and secondary) with pager contact and slack channel.

---

## 2) Acceptance matrix (hard gates)

Table: acceptance criteria that must be met to promote a model out of shadow. All thresholds are examples; teams should adapt per-product.

| Criterion | Target (example) | Measurement method | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 99th-percentile token latency (p99) | <= 450ms (hosted 16k context) | Synthetic microbenchmark with representative batching mix | infra/serving-runtime |
| Median per-token cost delta vs baseline | <= +10% | Tokenized replay cost model | finance/optimizer |
| Fidelity delta (F1 / BLEU / semantic-similarity) vs baseline | >= -3% absolute or within tolerance band | Anchor-based eval on fidelity prompts (see Sec 3) | applied-ml |
| Cache hit degradation | <= 5% absolute | Shadow traffic with traffic-mirroring and cache telemetry | eng-sre |
| Determinism on seed | identical responses for determinism probes | seeded replay | applied-ml |
\nNotes: Any single hard gate failure blocks promotion. Soft gates (e.g., cost improvements) may be acceptable if compensated by other benefits and with explicit approval.

---

## 3) Probe suite design: prompt families and slices

Design intent: prioritize slices that expose quantization sensitivity (e.g., tokens with rare subword patterns), and cache-bound behavior (long-context priming, multi-turn coherence). For each probe include: input prompt, expected anchor output, tolerance and failure modes.

Minimum probe families (suggested):
1. Short factual Q&A (latency-sensitive) — 1–3 tokens answer length, high precision requirement.
2. Multi-turn followup coherence (cache-sensitive) — 4–12 turn synthetic conversations with interleaved context that stresses KV reuse.
3. Long-context summarization (memory & quant-sensitivity) — 8–16k context summarization tasks.
4. Instruction-synthesis tasks (semantic fidelity) — open-ended responses scored by semantic-similarity + human spot-check.
5. Adversarial subword probes (quant-sensitivity) — tokens that force boundary-tokenization differences.

Each family must include:
- 500–2000 automated probes for automated acceptance, plus 50–200 human-reviewed anchors used for final approval.
- Metadata: seed_id, author, creation_date, expected metric and threshold.

---

## 4) Eval harness recipes (quant-aware & cache-aware)

A. Static quant validation (offline)
1. Run per-layer activation distribution checks with calibration dataset.
2. Compute per-prompt-family fidelity metrics using the quantized artifact.
3. Run bitflip sensitivity (small perturbations to calibration) to estimate fragility.

CLI example:

python tools/quant_eval.py --model artifacts/model-v2 --calib calib/seedset --slices long_context,adversarial --out reports/quant-v2.json

B. Cache-aware shadow replay (online)
1. Mirror 0.5–2% of production traffic to a shadow cluster configured with the quantized artifact and KV cache enabled.
2. Measure: response deltas, cache hit/miss rates, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and error rates.
3. Correlate errors with cache heatmap and tokenization drift tags.

Telemetry: ensure the shadow run produces the following time-series: cache_hit_rate, cache_miss_rate, kv_latency_ms, response_fidelity_delta. Plumb these into the eval dashboard.

C. Cost-sensitivity sweep
- Run batched synthetic load with varying batch sizes (1, 4, 8, 16) and sequence lengths representative of product workload.
- Produce a cost-latency curve and identify knee points where quantization no longer improves economics.

---

## 5) Rollout plan and guardrails (owner: infra + applied-ml)

Stages: 
- Shadow (no user-visible traffic) — required for all quantized artifacts. Minimum: 48–72h of shadow traffic covering peak and off-peak.
- Micro-canary (1% traffic) — 6–12h with strict telemetry gates.
- Canary (5–10%) — 24–48h with rolling increase and automated rollback on gate failures.
- Gradual rollout to 50% then 100% with staggered regional expansion.

Primary automated gates (examples):
- Fidelity regression: rolling 30-min window average <= threshold.
- Latency spike: p99 increase > +15% -> automatic pause.
- Error budget burn: >50% of daily error budget -> pause and notify.
- Cache degradation: sustained hit-rate drop > 7% for 30m -> rollback.

Rollback policy: automatic rollback to previous artifact on any hard gate failure. Human-in-the-loop: for soft-gate failures, require approval from applied-ml lead + oncall SRE.

---

## 6) Regression triage quick path (owner: oncall + applied-ml)

When a regression alert fires:
1. Triage channel & severity: create incident channel and assign severity.
2. Reproduce: run failing probes against both baseline and candidate artifacts.
3. Localize: compare per-layer activations, tokenization diffs, and cache hit traces.
4. Mitigate: possible fast mitigations include reverting quantized artifact, disabling KV cache for affected model, or switching traffic to higher-precision variant.
5. Postmortem: within 72h, publish an incident summary and update probe set if necessary.

Quick diagnostic checklist (commands):
- Replay failing prompt locally: python tools/replay.py --prompt-id 2345 --model artifacts/model-v2 --seed 42
- Dump activation diff: python tools/actdiff.py --base artifacts/model-v1 --cand artifacts/model-v2 --prompt 2345 --out actdiff/2345.json
- Inspect cache trace: curl -s "https://telemetry.redwood.internal/cache_trace?trace_id=abcd" | jq .

---

## 7) Common failure modes and recommended fixes

- Mode: tokenization boundary mismatch after quantization
  - Symptom: short factual answers truncated or off-by-words
  - Fix: re-run tokenizer alignment test, increase calibration set diversity, or pin to model variant with preserved tokenizer class.

- Mode: KV cache warmup causing latency spikes
  - Symptom: elevated tail latency for first requests after rollout
  - Fix: pre-warm hot prefixes via synthetic priming traffic or serve traffic through a regionally warmed pool.

- Mode: semantic drift in rare-token tails
  - Symptom: lower semantic-similarity on adversarial subword probes
  - Fix: add focused calibration examples, enable per-layer mixed-precision for embedding layers.

- Mode: quantized artifact shows nondeterministic outputs under multi-seed
  - Symptom: variance in deterministic probes
  - Fix: lock RNG seeds in runtime, validate FP emulation path, evaluate different quant backend.

---

## 8) Observability & dashboards (owner: eng-platform)

Minimum dashboards:
- Model health overview: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, traffic %, cache hit-rate, fidelity-delta time-series.
- Probe slice explorer: per-slice fidelity/time metrics with drilldown to failing probes.
- Cost curve: token-cost over time with batching and quantization toggles.

Alerts and escalation:
- Alert on any hard gate violation and route to applied-ml+oncall SRE.
- Automated runbooks contain pre-filled remediation steps and rollback commands.

---

## 9) Documentation & artifacts to commit

For audit and reproducibility, commit the following to the model onboarding folder in confluence and artifact registry:
- quantization manifest (algorithm, parameters, per-layer notes)
- probe suite manifest and seed lists
- shadow run report and telemetry export (48–72h)
- rollout plan with owners and contact details
- post-launch evaluation report (72h and 7-day summaries)

---

## 10) Appendix: sample probe manifest (JSON lines example)

{\n  "probe_id": "longctx-0001",\n  "family": "long_context_summarization",\n  "seed": "anon-seed-23",\n  "expected_metric": "semantic_similarity",\n  "tolerance": ">=0.82",\n  "notes": "Anchor derived from human summary v3"\n}

{\n  "probe_id": "adv-subword-0012",\n  "family": "adversarial_subword",\n  "seed": "adv-seed-12",\n  "expected_metric": "exact_match",\n  "tolerance": ">=0.95",\n  "notes": "Contains rare subword tokens; used to measure quant fragility"\n}

---

If you are the model owner starting a new quantized onboarding, follow the Pre-onboarding checklist and open a rollout ticket using the template in the related pages. For questions, ping @marissa.chen on #infra-ml or add reviewers listed above to your onboarding ticket.
